title: Fabrication and Application of Rose Bengal-chitosan Films in Laser Tissue Repair
protocol: Prepare a stock solution of acetic acid by adding 10 ml glacial acetic acid to 490 ml deionized water (DI-H2O).
Weigh 5 mg of Rose Bengal in a vial wrapped with aluminum foil to avoid photobleaching.
Add 0.5 ml of DI-H2O to the Rose Bengal powder and dissolve it.
Add 49.5 ml of acetic acid stock solution to the dissolved Rose Bengal to prepare a RB acetic acid stock solution (0.01% w/v).
Weigh 0.85 g of chitosan powder (medium MW, 85% degree of acetylation) and add it to 50 ml of RB acetic acid solution.
Add a magnetic stirrer to the chitosan mixture in the RB acetic acid solution and stir at room temperature for two weeks to ensure complete dissolution.

For the control preparation, dissolve 0.85 g of chitosan powder in 50 ml of pure acetic acid stock solution without Rose Bengal, then add a magnetic stirrer and stir at room temperature for five days to ensure complete dissolution.
Centrifuge the solutions at 3270 x g for 1 hr.
Collect the supernatant using a sterile 10 ml syringe.
Inject the centrifuged chitosan solution onto a flat perpex slab using a sterile syringe.
Ensure that the solution is free from air bubbles and evenly spread on the slab.
Cover the Perspex slab with a screen, such as aluminum foil, to avoid photobleaching of the solution.
Leave the solution to dry at room temperature (25 °C) and pressure (1 atm).
Detach the films carefully using a thin and flat spatula.
Measure the thickness of the films using a micrometer.
Cut the adhesive in rectangular strips using clean sharp scissors.
Place the adhesive between sterile glass slides.
Wrap the glass slides containing the adhesive in aluminum foil for light shielding.
Store wrapped slides at room temperature.
Label rose adhesives as "rose adhesive" and chitosan adhesives as "chitosan adhesive".
Sterilize rose adhesive films using ethanol (90%) or gamma radiation (0.1 KGy/h for 24 hr).
Fix the rose adhesive inside a quartz cuvette.
Record the attenuated spectrum of the rose adhesive from 400 to 800 nm.
Calculate the attenuation length of the rose adhesive according to Beer's law.
Repeat steps for fixing, recording spectra, and calculating attenuation for chitosan adhesive as control.
Harvest calf intestine immediately after animal euthanasia.
Store harvested intestine at -80°C until use.
Defrost and hydrate intestinal tissue by immersing it in DI-H2O for 10 min before use.
Bisect the hydrated tissue into sections (2 x 1 cm) using a #10 blade under an operating microscope at x10 magnification.
Keep bisected tissue sections moist with DI-H2O.
Bring incision stumps of intestinal sections close together (end to end).
Wipe excess water off the surface using cotton tips.
Place a rose adhesive strip across the incision on the serosa layer with microforceps ensuring full contact with the intestine.
Set the power level of the laser to 180 mW.
Irradiate the adhesive for ~6 min with a beam spot size of ~5 mm, using parameters listed in Table 1.
Spot-irradiate the adhesive, ensuring that each spot is irradiated for ~5 seconds before moving the beam to the adjacent spot.
Clamp a sample to a calibrated single column tensiometer using mechanical grips.
Move the grips at 22 mm/min until the two tissue stumps separate.
Place a rose adhesive on the tissue as described in step 3.5.
Do not irradiate the sample.
Measure the tissue bonding strength as described in step 3.8.
This sample serves as a control.
Sedate the Wistar rat with isoflurane/O2 mixture (4% during induction, 2% thereafter).
Subcutaneously inject Buprenex (0.03 mg/kg) to provide intra-operative analgesic activity and alleviate possible pain or discomfort.
Make an oblique skin incision about 3 cm long in the dorso-lateral part of the right thigh.
Expose the tibial nerve with a muscle-splitting approach through the gluteal muscles.
Partially dissect and trim the adventitia of the tibial nerve using straight micro-scissors.
Absorb excess water with sterile gauze or cotton tips.
Cut the tibial nerve with micro-scissors.
Position a sterile chitosan strip (dimensions 5 x 4 mm) underneath the tibial nerve using micro-forceps.
Approximate the nerve stumps end-to-end with micro-forceps over the rose adhesive strip.
Activate the rose adhesive with the laser as described in steps 3.6) and 3.7).
Trim the redundant rose adhesive from the collar of the operated nerve.
Close the muscles and skin with five 3-0 sutures.
Follow standard post-operative recovery procedures including daily inspection for dehiscence or pus formation.
Administer analgesics if required.
